answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Minting. Each identity is minted from a unique, verifiable training trajectory; agents must periodically sign a fresh challenge whose correct response depends on private update history that cannot be copied without replaying the full run. Clones cannot forge divergent responses, so a copied identity fails the basalt-anchored checkpoint. Each new identity therefore costs one full independent compute run plus storage of its delta, making mass duplication linear in real training cost rather than free.
